evidence: Plin. NH 35.76: praecipuē arithmēticā et geōmetriā
terms.comment: Greek ἀριθμητική, the art of numbers. Vitruvius declines it in Greek, arithmēticē, -ēs; Cicero says arithmētica, neuter plural (Att. 14.12.3).
Quintilian divides geometry, as mathematics was called, into numbers and figures (in numerōs atque fōrmās). Learning to count and reckon is numerāre discere (see count).

phrases.latin: ubi legere et scrībere et numerāre discitur
phrases.english: where one learns to read, to write and to count

phrases.latin: hominem remōtum ā dialecticīs, in arithmēticīs satis exercitātum
phrases.english: a man far from logic, but well practised in arithmetic (Cicero’s host, the banker Vestorius)
